facts.fact: The page states that Honduras opened its telecommunications sector to private investment on December 25, 2005, as required under CAFTA.
facts.quote: The telecommunications sector was opened for private investment on December 25, 2005, as required under CAFTA.

facts.fact: The page states that the price of gasoline in Honduras is regulated, and that Congress often regulates the temporary price of basic goods.
facts.quote: The price of gasoline is regulated, Congress often regulates the temporary price of basic goods.

facts.fact: The page describes San Pedro Sula as the largest business and commercial center in Honduras and as known as "La Capital Industrial".
facts.quote: San Pedro Sula is the largest business and commercial center in Honduras and is home to many major manufacturers and companies. It is usually called “La Capital Industrial”.

facts.fact: The page identifies ENEE (Empresa Nacional de Energía Eléctrica) as the government electricity grid operator and Hondutel as the online telephone service in Honduras.
facts.quote: The government uses both the electricity grid, the Empresa Nacional de Energygía Eléctrica (ENEE), and the online telephone service, Hondutel.
